title: Idli
instructions: Step 1: Soak rice and urad dal separately for 4-6 hours.
Step 2: Grind into a smooth batter and ferment overnight.
Step 3: Add salt and mix well.
Step 4: Steam in specialized molds or spread on a hot griddle with oil.
Step 5: Serve hot with fresh coconut chutney and piping hot sambar.

title: Chole Bhature
instructions: Step 1: Prepare a soft wheat dough and let it rest.
Step 2: Mash boiled ingredients and mix thoroughly with dry spices and chopped herbs.
Step 3: Stuff a small portion of the mixture into rolled dough rounds.
Step 4: Roll out gently and cook on a hot tawa with ghee until crispy golden.
Step 5: Serve warm with cold yogurt, pickle, or a dollop of white butter.

title: Dal Makhani
instructions: Step 1: Sauté chopped onions, ginger, garlic, and tomatoes until soft and completely cooked.
Step 2: Blend into a silky smooth paste and strain if desired.
Step 3: Cook the paste with aromatic dry spices and butter until oil starts to separate.
Step 4: Add the core protein/vegetables and simmer gently with water or cream.
Step 5: Garnish with a drizzle of heavy cream and crushed fenugreek leaves.

title: Kootu
instructions: Step 1: Boil the lentils and chopped vegetables separately until soft.
Step 2: Extract fresh tamarind juice and simmer it with turmeric and spice powders.
Step 3: Combine the cooked lentils, vegetables, and tamarind broth together.
Step 4: Prepare a tempering of mustard seeds, red chillies, and curry leaves in coconut oil.
Step 5: Pour the tempering over the hot curry and simmer for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Kosha Mangsho
instructions: Step 1: Marinate meat with yogurt, lime juice, ginger-garlic paste, and robust spices for 2 hours.
Step 2: Sear or grill the marinated meat pieces until partially or fully cooked.
Step 3: Prepare a rich base gravy by slow-cooking browned onions, tomato purée, and spices.
Step 4: Integrate the meat into the gravy and simmer on a low flame until perfectly tender.
Step 5: Adjust seasoning and finish with chopped fresh coriander or a dash of cream.

title: Shorshe Ilish
instructions: Step 1: Clean and prep the seafood or boil the eggs properly.

Step 4: Pour in coconut milk or tamarind extract and bring to a gentle boil.

title: Prawn Biryani
instructions: Step 1: Parboil long-grain basmati rice with whole spices until 70% cooked.

Step 2: Dry roast peanuts, sesame seeds, coconut, and coriander seeds; grind into a thick spice paste.

Step 2: Heat ghee in a pan, sauté cumin seeds, garlic, ginger, and chopped onions until golden.
Step 3: Add diced tomatoes, red chilli powder, and cook until tomatoes turn soft and mushy.
Step 4: Pour cooked dal into the gravy, add water to adjust consistency and simmer for 5 minutes.
Step 5: Top with a final ghee tadka of garlic and red chilli powder. Serve hot with jeera rice or naan!

title: Gujarati Sweet Dal
instructions: Step 1: Knead milk solids (khoya) with a pinch of flour into a soft, smooth dough without cracks.
Step 2: Prepare warm sugar syrup flavoured with crushed cardamom strands and saffron.
Step 3: Shape dough into small round balls.
Step 4: Heat pure ghee in a pan on low-medium flame; fry balls gently until rich golden brown.
Step 5: Drop hot fried jamuns directly into warm sugar syrup; let soak for 2 hours until juicy and soft!

title: Hyderabadi Dum Biryani
instructions: Step 1: Wash and soak basmati rice for 30 minutes; boil with whole spices until 80% cooked.
Step 2: Sauté thin sliced onions in ghee until deep golden brown (Birista).
Step 3: Cook main gravy with yogurt, ginger-garlic, mint, coriander, and biryani masala.
Step 4: Layer cooked rice over gravy, top with fried onions, mint, saffron milk, and ghee.
Step 5: Cover tightly with foil/dough lid and dum cook on low flame for 15 minutes. Serve with raita!

title: Paneer Butter Masala
instructions: Step 1: Cut paneer into cubes and soak in warm water for 5 minutes to stay soft.
Step 2: Melt butter in a pan, sauté onions and ginger-garlic paste until golden brown.
Step 3: Add fresh tomato puree, chilli powder, coriander powder, and cook until butter separates.
Step 4: Add paneer cubes, fresh cream, crushed kasuri methi, and simmer gently for 5 minutes.
Step 5: Garnish with fresh cream and coriander. Serve hot with butter naan or lacchha paratha!
